title: ONNX networks can't use INT8 calibration and batching
author: gcp
body: Description This is due to mutually incompatible changes in the TRT7 release: https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/sdk/tensorrt-release-notes/tensorrt-7.html  ONNX parser with dynamic shapes support The ONNX parser supports full-dimensions mode only. Your network definition must be created with the explicitBatch flag set.  versus  Known Issues The INT8 calibration does not work with dynamic shapes. To workaround this issue, ensure there are two passes in the code: Using a fixed shape input to build the engine in the first pass, allows TensorRT to generate the calibration cache.  This means the ONNX network must be exported at a fixed batch size in order to get INT8 calibration working, but now it's no longer possible to specify the batch size. I also verified that manually fixing up the inputs with setDimensions(...-1...) does not work, you will hit an assertion  mg.nodes[mg.regionIndices[outputRegion]].size ==mg.nodes[mg.regionIndices[inputRegion]].size while building. One would think there might be sort of a workaround by exporting two different networks, one with a fixed batch size and a second one with a dynamic_axis, and then using the calibration from one for the other. However, even here there are severe pitfalls: a calibration cache that is generated for, say, batch_size=1 won't necessarily work for larger batch sizes, presumably because they will generate a different convolution strategy that causes different accuracy issues. Edit: This might've been another issue. Lastly, the calibrator itself appears to be using implicit batch sizes, and breaks on batch size > 1 as follows: TRT: Starting Calibration with batch size 16. Calibrated 16 images. TRT: Explicit batch network detected and batch size specified, use execute without batch size instead. TRT: C:\source\builder\cudnnCalibrator.cpp (707) - Cuda Error in nvinfer1::builder::Histogram::add: 700 (an illegal memory access was encountered) TRT: FAILED_ALLOCATION: Unknown exception TRT: C:\source\builder\cudnnCalibrator.cpp (703) - Cuda Error in nvinfer1::builder::Histogram::add: 700 (an illegal memory access was encountered) TRT: FAILED_ALLOCATION: Unknown exception TRT: C:\source\rtSafe\cuda\caskConvolutionRunner.cpp (233) - Cuda Error in nvinfer1::rt::task::CaskConvolutionRunner::allocateContextResources: 700 (an illegal memory access was encountered) TRT: FAILED_EXECUTION: Unknown exception TRT:   Calibrated batch 0 in 2.62865 seconds. Cuda failure: 700 with batch_size == 1, it's also hitting assertions: TRT: Explicit batch network detected and batch size specified, use execute without batch size instead. TRT: Assertion failed: d.nbDims >= 1 C:\source\rtSafe\safeHelpers.cpp:419 Aborting... The combination of all these failures means that you can't really use ONNX networks in INT8 mode, at least the "Using a fixed shape input to build the engine in the first pass" recommendation hits all kinds of internal assertions as you can see above. body: Description Tensorflow's network structure definition is relatively redundant compared to Caffe. I wish TensorRT can remove these redundancies for inference acceleration. By the way, the tested model is fully constitutional network, It has been converted to dynamic shape model when testing. title: Inconsistent documentation on max_workspace_size
author: gcp
body: Description According to the TensorRT documentation: https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/sdk/tensorrt-developer-guide/index.html#build_engine_python you have to set the max_workspace_size on the builder object. However, empirically, when using ONNX networks, I see in the verbose TensorRT logging that strategies aren't tried because there is 0 workspace available. Despite it being set to 2**31. Now, if you look at other TensorRT docs: https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/sdk/tensorrt-api/python_api/infer/Core/NetworkConfig.html You see that there's a "new" max_workspace_size on the config object of the builder. Empirically, setting that one does work. The documentation seems inconsistent and wrong here. It's somewhat likely people are going to get performance regressions with TensorRT 7 because they're accidentally building engines with no workspace? Environment TensorRT Version:  7.0.0.11 GPU Type:  GTX 1060 Nvidia Driver Version:  440.36 CUDA Version:  10.2 CUDNN Version:  7.6.0.3 Operating System + Version:  Ubuntu 18.04 Python Version (if applicable):  3.6 TensorFlow Version (if applicable): PyTorch Version (if applicable):  1.3 stable Baremetal or Container (if container which image + tag):  bare Relevant Files https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/sdk/tensorrt-developer-guide/index.html#build_engine_python https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/sdk/tensorrt-api/python_api/infer/Core/NetworkConfig.html

title: Issue using slice layer to get the only the CLS embedding from BERT
author: churinga
body: Description BERT output has the following dims: (batchsize, maxseqlen, hiddensize, 1, 1). We want to map it to (batchsize, 1, hiddensize, 1, 1), so that only the [0] index of maxseqlen dimension (i.e. the CLS embedding output) will be used in the softmax layer. The problem is that the tensor shape of bert_out.shape[0] is -1, i.e. batchsize is not static. And ISliceLayer does not accept negative value in the shape parameter. It will complain as follows: [TensorRT] INTERNAL ERROR: Assertion failed: dims.d[i] >= 1 ../builder/cudnnBuilderGraph.cpp:605 Aborting...  [TensorRT] ERROR: ../builder/cudnnBuilderGraph.cpp (605) - Assertion Error in checkDimsSanity: 0 (dims.d[i] >= 1)  Here is the code: # bert_out is the BERT embedding output, with shape (-1, maxseqlen, hiddensize, 1, 1) bert_out = bert_model(config, init_dict, network, embeddings, mask_idx) cls_embed = network.add_slice(bert_out, start=(0,0,0,0,0), shape=(-1,1,hiddensize,1,1), stride=(1,1,1,1,1)) So, is there a way to do the slicing gracefully by honoring the batch size? Thanks! Environment TensorRT Version: 19.10 GPU Type: NVIDIA T4 Nvidia Driver Version: 418.116.00 CUDA Version: 10.1 CUDNN Version: 7.6.5.32-1 Operating System + Version: RHEL7.6 Python Version (if applicable): 3.6.8 TensorFlow Version (if applicable): 1.14.0 PyTorch Version (if applicable): N/A Baremetal or Container (if container which image + tag): Container

title: There is a bug in  TensorRT/samples/opensource/sampleUffMaskRCNN/converted/0001-Update-the-Mask_RCNN-model-from-NHWC-to-NCHW.patch
author: hwh-hit
body: Description First i find that trt sampleUffMaskrcnn has a different result with maskrcnn implemented in keras. I print the output layer by layer . finally I find and solved the problem, There is a bug in the patched code. @kevinch-nv @rmccorm4 , we should add x = KL.Permute((2,3,1))(x) in https://github.com/matterport/Mask_RCNN/blob/3deaec5d902d16e1daf56b62d5971d428dc920bc/mrcnn/model.py#L867 before rpn_bbox = KL.Reshape((-1, 4))(x). If not, the output of rpn_bbox is wrong. so we can't get the exactly same result with keras in NHWC format

title: Empty Tensor Support
author: 1-800-BAD-CODE
body: Description I have a network that takes as input a tensor that may have a little as zero elements in one dimension, therefore the optimization profile must have a minimum of zero. title: Mobilenet ONNX model network validation fails with TensorRT 7 after adding the EXPLICIT_BATCH network definition flag
author: svnoesis
body: Description While running inference with Mobilenetv1 using onnx model file on TensorRT 7, the network validation failed. The model works fine on TensorRT 6.0.1. When moving to TensorRT 7.0.0.11, it gave the error ""This version of the ONNX parser only supports TensorRT INetworkDefinitions with an explicit batch dimension." Hence added the EXPLICIT_BATCH flag when parsing the ONNX model to create the network as discussed in #358 After adding the EXPLICIT_BATCH flag it throws below error during calibration phase when builder.build_engine is invoked. [TensorRT] ERROR: fc_replaced: kernel weights has count 1024000 but 1048576000 was expected [TensorRT] ERROR: fc_replaced: count of 1024000 weights in kernel, but kernel dimensions (1,1) with 1024 input channels, 1024000 output channels and 1 groups were specified. Expected Weights count is 1024 * 1*1 * 1024000 / 1 = 1048576000 [TensorRT] ERROR: fc_replaced: kernel weights has count 1024000 but 1048576000 was expected [TensorRT] ERROR: fc_replaced: count of 1024000 weights in kernel, but kernel dimensions (1,1) with 1024 input channels, 1024000 output channels and 1 groups were specified. Expected Weights count is 1024 * 1*1 * 1024000 / 1 = 1048576000 [TensorRT] ERROR: Layer fc_replaced failed validation [TensorRT] ERROR: Network validation failed.  The above error is due to how the tensorrt layers are created in the network in TensorRT7. Logging the layers after network creation showed that there is a difference in how the layers are generated in TRT6 and TRT7. In the code, after parsing the onnx model, it looks for Matrix Multiply layer and it is replaced with a Conv layer. For that it reads the weights from the previous layers and calculates the weights required for the new "fc_replaced" layer and adds the new layer to the network. This calculation of weights goes wrong because the layers are now different in TRT7 compared to TRT6. Hence the above error. This looks to be a issue on TRT7 and breaks existing workloads. Will TRT7 not be backward compatible for workloads that were running with TensorRT 6 ? title: Enhancement: add nvprof mode to trtexec
author: ryanolson
body: I appreciate the dumpProfile and exportProfile option available in trtexec; however, those options only provide the layer descriptions and timings, but not the names of the actual kernels being executed. To determine the precision types of kernels being selected by the builder and evaluated at runtime, one still needs to use nvprof to extract a profile. To simplify the output from the profiler, I'm requesting that the cuda profile api is used to disable profiling during setup and tear down and only enable profile around the execution of the engine. #include <cuda_profiler_api.h> ...  cudaProfilerStart(); doInference(); cudaProfilerStop();  Example: nvprof trtexec --useCudaGraph --iterations=1 --warmUp=0 --duration=0 --loadEngine=my_awesome_dnn.engine

Segfault code build_engine.py def define_network(builder, args, cfg, plugins):     explicit_batch = 1 << int(trt.NetworkDefinitionCreationFlag.EXPLICIT_BATCH)     network = builder.create_network(explicit_batch)     define_mbert(network, args, cfg, plugins)   # FOCUS     return network  def main(args):     cfg = load_config(args.config_file)     builder = get_builder(args)     plugins = get_plugins()     network = define_network(builder, args, cfg, plugins)   # FOCUS     profiles = get_profiles(builder, args, cfg)     config = get_config(builder, profiles, args)     engine = builder.build_engine(network, config)     with open(args.out_engine_path, "wb") as f:         f.write(engine.serialize()) model.py def define_mbert(net, args, cfg, plugins):     w_dict = get_weights(args.weight_pth_file)   # FOCUS     inps = _get_inputs(net, inp_len=cfg['max_position_embeddings'])     embedded, inp_mask = embedding(net, w_dict, args, plugins, inps)     enc_out = bert(net, w_dict, args, cfg, embedded, inps[2], plugins)     net.mark_output(enc_out) Nice code build_engine.py def define_network(builder, w_dict, args, cfg, plugins):     explicit_batch = 1 << int(trt.NetworkDefinitionCreationFlag.EXPLICIT_BATCH)     network = builder.create_network(explicit_batch)     define_mbert(network, w_dict, args, cfg, plugins)   # FOCUS     return network  def main(args):     cfg = load_config(args.config_file)     builder = get_builder(args)     plugins = get_plugins()     w_dict = get_weights(args.weight_pth_file)   # FOCUS     network = define_network(builder, w_dict, args, cfg, plugins)   # FOCUS     profiles = get_profiles(builder, args, cfg)     config = get_config(builder, profiles, args)     engine = builder.build_engine(network, config)     with open(args.out_engine_path, "wb") as f:         f.write(engine.serialize()) model.py def define_mbert(net, w_dict, args, cfg, plugins):     inps = _get_inputs(net, inp_len=cfg['max_position_embeddings'])     embedded, inp_mask = embedding(net, w_dict, args, plugins, inps)     enc_out = bert(net, w_dict, args, cfg, embedded, inps[2], plugins)     net.mark_output(enc_out) Can you see? Yup, in my case, segfault issue was caused by lifetime of w_dict. w_dict was deallocated automatically before builder::buildCudaEngine() call and segfault occured since C 's void pointer also use same memory address. I hope this little tip helps someone. Regards, Anthony.

title: TensorRT is Unable to convert the FusedBatchNormV2 op
author: danfischetti
body: Description TensorRT is unable to convert the FusedBatchNormV2 op. When I turn on verbose logging I see messages like this: 2020-03-14 17:28:54.501494: I tensorflow/compiler/tf2tensorrt/segment/segment.cc:439] Not a TF-TRT candidate, (Op type: FusedBatchNormV2), (Op name: pose/pose/resnet_v2_50/block1/unit_1/bottleneck_v2/preact/FusedBatchNormV2), (Reason: Unimplemented: FusedBatchNormV2 only supports data_format=NCHW, at pose/pose/resnet_v2_50/block1/unit_1/bottleneck_v2/preact/FusedBatchNormV2)  I explicitly converted my graph to use the channels first data format after seeing channels_last was not supported for batch norm with TensorRT. I also confirmed that the frozen graph saves the node definitions in NCHW form. Inspecting the node referenced in the log message shows: name: "pose/pose/resnet_v2_50/block1/unit_1/bottleneck_v2/preact/FusedBatchNormV2" op: "FusedBatchNormV2" input: "pose/pose/resnet_v2_50/pool1/MaxPool" input: "pose/resnet_v2_50/block1/unit_1/bottleneck_v2/preact/gamma/read" input: "pose/resnet_v2_50/block1/unit_1/bottleneck_v2/preact/beta/read" input: "pose/resnet_v2_50/block1/unit_1/bottleneck_v2/preact/moving_mean/read" input: "pose/resnet_v2_50/block1/unit_1/bottleneck_v2/preact/moving_variance/read" attr {   key: "T"   value {     type: DT_HALF   } } attr {   key: "U"   value {     type: DT_FLOAT   } } attr {   key: "data_format"   value {     s: "NCHW"   } } attr {   key: "epsilon"   value {     f: 1.001e-05   } } attr {   key: "is_training"   value {     b: false   } }  So the data_format is correct and is_training is false, so I would expect TensorRT to be able to convert this node. Environment TensorRT Version: 6.0.1.10 GPU Type: Jetson Xavier Nvidia Driver Version: CUDA Version: 10.0 CUDNN Version: 7.6.3 Operating System + Version: Ubuntu 18.04 Python Version (if applicable): 3.6.9 TensorFlow Version: 1.15 Baremetal or Container (if container which image + tag):  Baremetal I've managed to reproduce the issue with a minimal script and tracked down when the issue occurs. Adding a batch_norm operation inside a convolution layer is what leads to the issue. I've included a sample script to reproduce the problem. import argparse from make_tf_model import output_tensor_names from tensorflow.python.compiler.tensorrt import trt_convert as trt import tensorflow as tf import datetime from tensorflow.python.compat import compat import tensorflow.contrib.slim as slim   def main():     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()     parser.add_argument("--with_conv", action="store_true")     args = parser.parse_args()     with_conv = args.with_conv     compat._update_forward_compatibility_date_number(datetime.date(2019, 6, 6)) # force tensorflow to use FusedBatchNormV2     with tf.Session() as sess:         input0 = tf.placeholder(tf.float16, [10, 3, 224, 224])         out = input0          out = slim.batch_norm(out, data_format="NCHW", scope="bn1", is_training=False)         out = slim.batch_norm(out, data_format="NHWC", scope="bn2", is_training=False)         with slim.arg_scope([slim.conv2d, slim.batch_norm], data_format="NCHW"), slim.arg_scope([slim.batch_norm], is_training=False):             if with_conv:                 out = slim.conv2d(out, 64, [3, 3], normalizer_fn=slim.batch_norm)         out = tf.identity(out)         out_name = out.name[:-2]          init = tf.global_variables_initializer()         sess.run(init)          frozen_graph = tf.graph_util.convert_variables_to_constants(                 sess, tf.get_default_graph().as_graph_def(), output_node_names=[out_name])          with tf.gfile.GFile(f"/home/standard/minimal{'_with_conv' if with_conv else ''}.pb", "wb") as f:             f.write(frozen_graph.SerializeToString())          converter = trt.TrtGraphConverter(             input_graph_def=frozen_graph,             nodes_blacklist=[out_name],             max_batch_size=10, max_workspace_size_bytes=5000000000,             maximum_cached_engines=256,             precision_mode="FP16", is_dynamic_op=True)         trt_graph = converter.convert()          with tf.gfile.GFile("/home/standard/dummy.pb", "wb") as f:             f.write(trt_graph.SerializeToString())   if __name__ == "__main__":     main() Running this script without the with_conv flag leads to expected results. I've included a NCHW batch norm and a NHWC batch norm to demonstrate that TensorRT has no problem changing the layout of the op. title: fp16 mode takes much more time than fp32
author: yizhaoyanbo
body: Jatson TX2 8G CUDA 10.2 TensorRT 7.0 cudnn 7.6 onnx IR verison 0.0.4 opset version 9 pytorch verson 1.2 I get onnx model from pytorch. And it runs successfully on tx2 board with 30ms per frame. So I want to try fp16 mode to  accelerate the prediction. The configurations I have set are as follows config->setFlag(BuilderFlag::kGPU_FALLBACK);   config->setFlag(BuilderFlag::kSTRICT_TYPES); if (mParams.fp16) {     config->setFlag(BuilderFlag::kFP16);  }  Then I find that fp16 mode takes about 90ms per frame with the same input. I have used the profiler API reportLayerTime() to get every layer's time. And I find that there are two main reasons:  The first reason is that there are many new layers which named input reformatter in fp16 mode, and these layers take a lot of time in prediction about 5% for my model. The second reason is that some layers take 10x ~ 40x time than fp32, such as the 10th row of the following picture(layer11[Convolution] + layer13[Activation], fp16-13ms, fp32-0.85ms). And it is the main reason which affect the prediction speed.  When the fp16 mode is running, the following log occurs. I don't understand what the log means. [trt log]: No implementation obeys reformatting-free rules, at least 4 reformatting nodes are needed, now picking the fastest path instead.  So How can I avoid to use these layers or use other method to accelerate the prediction in fp16 mode? The following image is the comparasion of profiler data, left is fp16 and right is fp32.

title: Bug with ReLU followed by adding Tensors (converting from pytorch)
author: HeekonKim
body: Description  Hi, I am using TensorRT converting from pytorch and I found that my model behaves quite different with PyTorch/ONNX when converted to TensorRT. After investigating the issue, I found that ReLU operation does not apply appropriately at specific situations. (In my case within residual block) ReLU operation is ignored when followed by adding Tensors. Environment TensorRT Version: 7.0.1.1 GPU Type: GTX 1080 Ti Nvidia Driver Version: 440.3.01 CUDA Version: 10.2 CUDNN Version: 7.6.5 Operating System + Version: ubuntu 16.04 Python Version (if applicable): 2.7 TensorFlow Version (if applicable): X PyTorch Version (if applicable): 1.5 Baremetal or Container (if container which image + tag): X Relevant Files  Steps To Reproduce  simple code below should reproduce this issue. import torch import torch.nn as nn import torch.nn.functional as F from torch2trt import torch2trt from torch2trt.torch2trt import *   torch.manual_seed(0)  class NonPoolingBlock(nn.Module):     def __init__(self, in_channel, mid_channel, filter_size=3, padding=1):         super(NonPoolingBlock, self).__init__()         self.block1 = ConvBlock(in_channel, mid_channel)         self.block2 = ConvBlock(mid_channel, in_channel)      def forward(self, x):         return x+ (self.block2(self.block1(x)))   class ConvBlock(nn.Module):     def __init__(self, in_channel, out_channel, filter_size=3, padding=1, stride=1):         super(ConvBlock, self).__init__()         self.conv = nn.Conv2d(in_channel, out_channel, filter_size, padding=padding, stride=stride)         self.conv_bn = nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channel)      def forward(self, x):         x = F.relu(self.conv_bn(self.conv(x)))         return x  net = NonPoolingBlock(4,4).eval().cuda() data = torch.ones((1,4,1,1)).cuda() model_trt = torch2trt(net,[data])  print(net(data)) print(model_trt(data)) print(torch.max(torch.abs(model_trt(data) - net(data))))  Output looks like below. tensor([[[[1.0527]],          [[1.0000]],          [[1.0000]],          [[1.0000]]]], device='cuda:0', grad_fn=<AddBackward0>) tensor([[[[1.0527]],          [[0.9966]],          [[0.9625]],          [[0.8973]]]], device='cuda:0') tensor(0.1027, device='cuda:0', grad_fn=<MaxBackward1>)  If you pad some operations after relu, like padding useless leaky_relu, relu applys well.

title: No speedup on batch size larger than 1
author: prathik-naidu
body: I've setup tensorRT to work on my yolov3 model where I'm running inference on each frame of a video stream. When I run with a single video stream and process each frame one at at time, I notice that the tensorRT version of the model gets a solid speedup over the regular model (going from 43 fps to 57 fps). However, when I try to process frames from larger batch sizes, like 5 different videos (and batch together 1 frame from each video into a batch size of 5), I don't see any speedup with tensorRT. I'm trying to understand why I see a speedup with batch size of 1 vs a batch size of 5. Any ideas why this might be happening or what I can look into for improving batch performance? I'm running with float 32 but would still expect a speedup for larger batch sizes for the tensorRT model. Here is an outline of my steps for creating and running the tensorRT engine:  Export yolo model to onnx using torch.onnx.export with the dynamic batches param Convert onnx to tensorRT engine  parse onnx model create a single optimization profile for a specific batch size: profile.set_shape(inp.name, min=(batch_size, *shape), opt=(batch_size, *shape), max=(batch_size, *shape)) build engine   Load the tensorRT engine + context  select the right tensorRT engine based on input batch size to inference function Set the binding shape: context.set_binding_shape(0, (BATCH_SIZE, 3, IMAGE_SIZE))  Set the optimization profile: context.active_optimization_profile = 0    Not sure if there's anything else I should be doing but these steps seem to be fine for handling inference with larger batch sizes. I'm running this on the latest TensorRT version.

title: Make samples stand-alone (no "common" folder)
author: justinblaber
body: General question, why is there this sub library ("common") for the code samples? If we want to see a minimal working example, for example loading and performing inference for an ONNX model, we have to go through, parse all this extra non-tensorRT code just to get a simple example working. The code for samples shouldn't be refactored really at all... each sample should be independent so people can pull that one example and easily mess around with it for their needs. Otherwise we would have to compile and add the common.h header to our code (or piece it up) which is not ideal. title: TensorRT does not support InstanceNorm3d
author: ranlu
body: Description Our model in pytorch contains serveral InstanceNorm3d operators. When I tried to load the onnx model using onnx-tensorrt, I get an assert error:  TensorRT only supports InstanceNormalization on 3D or 4D tensors! title: TensorRT NOT match result from pytorch quantization
author: leiwen83
body: Hi, I am trying to convert onnx model with TensorRT. But there is something internal I don't quite understand. That is as below graph shows, before entering the CONV stage, the input need to be adjust for quatization.  And I could see from the memory dump that tensorRT would amplify the input by [1/0.007874015718698502] which is the yscale parameter for the QuantizeLinear. Following in CONV, tensorRT do the int8 multiply and int32 accumulation. But before it leave the CONV, and ready to re-quantization into float32 again, I see there is a scale down operation, which make int32 fallen into int8 scale. The scale down parameter is taken from TRT generated engine, which I cannot find in the onnx model. So the first question is how TensorRT calculate the scale down for CONV layer from int32 to int8 in its last stage. title: [Question] What is the best scenario to use TRT with pytorch quantized model (QAT).
author: dhkim0225
body: Hello, I am an avid user who is using TensorRT for service. I want to serve the QAT model (int8) with TensorRT which is learned with pytorch 1.7.1. What is the best scenario to serve this model ? After some search time, I could find the following information. Please let me know, if I have a wrong information.  TensorRT has the pytorch-quantization v2.0.0 package. (from 7.2.1) The QAT of pytorch is still in beta, and the save format is constantly changing. (There is a version dependency.) Pytorch supports per tensor and per channel asymmetric method, but TensorRT supports per tensor method.   PyTorch supports both per tensor and per channel asymmetric linear quantization. Per tensor means that all the values within the tensor are scaled the same way. Per channel means that for each dimension, typically the channel dimension of a tensor, the values in the tensor are scaled and offset by a different value (effectively the scale and offset become vectors). This allows for lesser error in converting tensors to quantized values.  I'm totally having no idea which features should I use for QAT model serving with nvidia GPU (T4). Regards, Anthony Kim

title: pytorch-quantization examples are incompatible with latest torchvision reference scripts API
author: sjain-stanford
body: Description The example notebooks in pytorch-quantization such as calibrate_quant_resnet50.ipynb rely on convenience methods from torchvision's train.py - such as evaluate, train_one_epoch, and load_data. The functional signatures of some of these methods changed in latest torchvision and that breaks the notebooks. For example: Old def load_data(traindir, valdir, cache_dataset, distributed):  New def load_data(traindir, valdir, args):  As a temporary fix, reverting to this hash works: git checkout 24f16a338391d6f45aa6291c48eb6d5513771631

title: Quantization Error Analysis on Object Detection
author: JosephChenHub
body: Description When doing INT8 PTQ (post-training quantization), we notice that the dropout of the accuracy on image classification or semantic segmentation is rather small. However,  for the detectors like yolov5, there exists a huge gap of mAP between FP16 model and INT8 model. The comparison results are listed as the following,  e.g., for YOLOv5s, the mAP on COCO validation set decreases from 0.362 to 0.054 (or 0.316,  0.054 is the result of original onnx graph and 0.316 the result of custom plugin of SiLU).  The huge gap between 0.362 and 0.054 makes the model unreliable, and we observed that the yolov5s model utilizes an activation function SiLU (SiLU(x) = x * sigmoid(x)) which may reduce the accuracy due to its nonlinearity.  Hence, we manually write a plugin SiLU to replace the origin operator sigmoid and mul in the onnx graph, which looks like   As a result, we can see from the above table that our detector keeps stable and there still exists a little gap between the FP16 models and the INT8 model (for yolov5s, the mAP/FPS improves from 0.054/464 to 0.316/327 due to our custom plugin). Furthermore, we do partial quantization (use top 5 sensitive conv. layers) and the mAP is 0.332, which is still lower than 0.362. So questions come that  In the origin implementation, we see the log Layer(PointWiseV2): PWN(Sigmoid_213, Mul_214), Tactic: 24, 345[Int8(128,40,40)] -> 347[Int8(128,40,40)] , and how the TensorRT implements the INT8 operation on this layer (sigmoid + mul) ? In our own custom plugin, we implement the SiLU as  template <typename T> __device__ T _silu_op(const T input);  template <> __device__  __forceinline__ float _silu_op(const float input) {      return input / (static_cast<float>(1) + __expf(-input)); } template <> __device__  __forceinline__ __half _silu_op(const __half input) {     typedef __half T;     return input / (static_cast<T>(1) + hexp(-input)); }  template <typename T> __global__ void _kernel(const T* __restrict__ inputs, T* __restrict__ outputs, const size_t n ) {      const size_t tid = threadIdx.x + blockIdx.x * blockDim.x;     if (tid < n) {         outputs[tid] = _silu_op<T>(inputs[tid]);     }    }  does there exist a faster way to achieve this op?  or TensorRT will optimize this op like ReLU, Sigmoid in future ? 3. We notice that the sensitive layers usually are the first or last several conv. layers in the CNN, and the nonlinear modules are also sensitive. Is the error of PTQ mainly caused by the nonlinearity when doing linear quantization?  How to prevent that ? As far as we know, the QAT (quantization aware training) of TensorRT is still not applicable. The dropout of accuracy makes the QAT more desirable. When will TensorRT support QAT well ? title: After runing buildCudaEngine function, the nvidia driver crash down
author: wujixiu
body: Description  When I try to run TensorRT buildCudaEngine funtion to build the inference engine, the nvidia driver crash down and the computer also shut down too. This happens when I run the function in the following environment. However, when I run in the 1060 GPU with other software version is the same, everything works. I try to use cuda-gdb to debug the program, the program crash down after throwing a wraning "warning: Corrupted shared library list: 0x436ceab0 != 0x1332cf90", but in 1060 GPU this warning doesn't happend.      nvinfer1::INetworkDefinition *network = builder->createNetworkV2(explicitBatch);      std::cout << "createParser..." << std::endl;     nvonnxparser::IParser *parser = nvonnxparser::createParser(*network, gLogger_);      std::cout << "descryptModel..." << std::endl;     if (use_encrypt) {         if (!parser->parse(buffer, size)) {             std::cerr << MSG_HEAD << "failed to parse model file, please check and update your model";         }     }      std::cout << "resizeInput..." << std::endl;     if (length > 0 && width > 0) {         // resize input size         nvinfer1::ITensor *input_tensor = network->getInput(0);         nvinfer1::Dims dims = input_tensor->getDimensions();     builder->setFp16Mode(use_fp16_);     builder->setMaxBatchSize(1);     builder->setMaxWorkspaceSize(size_t(1) << max_workspace_);      std::cout << "buildCudaEngine..." << std::endl;     // the program crash down heare     nvinfer1::ICudaEngine *engine_init = builder->buildCudaEngine(*network); title: BERT demo causes memory leak
author: CourierKyn
body: Description Simply edit demo/BERT/inference_c.py line 211 to:             while True:                 inference(features, doc_tokens) As it loops, the container memory will run out and python got killed. Environment TensorRT Version: 7.2.2.3 NVIDIA GPU: Tesla T4 NVIDIA Driver Version: 460.32.03 CUDA Version: 11.2 CUDNN Version: 8.0.5 Operating System: ubuntu 18.04 Python Version (if applicable): python 3.6 Tensorflow Version (if applicable): 2.4.1 PyTorch Version (if applicable): n/a Baremetal or Container (if so, version): Docker version 19.03.1, build 74b1e89 Relevant Files demo/BERT/inference_c.py Steps To Reproduce Simply edit demo/BERT/inference_c.py line 211 to:             while True:                 inference(features, doc_tokens) Then follow the official instruction to start the script: python3 inference_c.py -e /workspace/TensorRT/demo/BERT/engines/bert_large_128.engine --enable-graph -p "TensorRT is a high performance deep learning inference platform that delivers low latency and high throughput for apps such as recommenders, speech and image/video on NVIDIA GPUs. It includes parsers to import models, and plugins to support novel ops and layers before applying optimizations for inference. Today NVIDIA is open-sourcing parsers and plugins in TensorRT so that the deep learning community can customize and extend these components to take advantage of powerful TensorRT optimizations for your apps." -q "What is TensorRT?" -v /workspace/TensorRT/demo/BERT/models/fine-tuned/bert_tf_ckpt_large_qa_squad2_amp_128_v19.03.1/vocab.txt

title: TensorRT 7.2 not setting Resize output shape when parsing ONNX
author: timsean
body: Description The ONNX parser that comes with TensorRT 7.2.2.1 is not computing the output of a Resize layer even when the output tensor's shape is defined. This issue is likely the same one from #440. I created a simple network using the ONNX Python API (Opset V13). The resulting network contains a single Resize node defined with a constant size input. This is the Netron visualization of the network.  When parsing the ONNX model, the output shape ends up as (-1, -1, -1, -1). [TensorRT] VERBOSE: /workspace/TensorRT/parsers/onnx/ModelImporter.cpp:183:  [Constant] outputs: [resize_size -> (4)],  [TensorRT] VERBOSE: /workspace/TensorRT/parsers/onnx/ModelImporter.cpp:107: Parsing node:  [Resize] [TensorRT] VERBOSE: /workspace/TensorRT/parsers/onnx/ModelImporter.cpp:123: Searching for input: input [TensorRT] VERBOSE: /workspace/TensorRT/parsers/onnx/ModelImporter.cpp:123: Searching for input: resize_size [TensorRT] VERBOSE: /workspace/TensorRT/parsers/onnx/ModelImporter.cpp:129:  [Resize] inputs: [input -> (1, 3, 128, 256)], [optional input, not set], [optional input, not set], [resize_size -> (4)],  [TensorRT] VERBOSE: /workspace/TensorRT/parsers/onnx/ImporterContext.hpp:154: Registering layer: node_of_output for ONNX node: node_of_output [TensorRT] VERBOSE: /workspace/TensorRT/parsers/onnx/ImporterContext.hpp:150: Registering constant layer: resize_size for ONNX initializer: resize_size [TensorRT] VERBOSE: /workspace/TensorRT/parsers/onnx/ImporterContext.hpp:120: Registering tensor: output_0 for ONNX tensor: output [TensorRT] VERBOSE: /workspace/TensorRT/parsers/onnx/ModelImporter.cpp:183:  [Resize] outputs: [output -> (-1, -1, -1, -1)],  [TensorRT] VERBOSE: /workspace/TensorRT/parsers/onnx/ModelImporter.cpp:538: Marking output_0 as output: output  Even though the TensorRT engine can be created successfully here, this causes some problems in more complex models, especially those that deal with plugins. It forces plugins to use IPluginV2DynamicExt even though when the network doesn't actually contain any dynamic shapes. I'm not sure if this is considered as a bug given that it doesn't actually stop TensorRT from building an engine. This may be just a missing implementation. title: Output from ONNX inference and trt inference are different
author: hoangmt
body: I am having problem with converting onnx model to tensorrt. Specifically, the results when inferred by the two models are different. Running onnx model code: import onnxruntime as rt import numpy as np sess = rt.InferenceSession('efficientdet-d0_nwonly.onnx') img=np.ones((1, 512, 512, 3),dtype=np.float32) y=sess.run(['output_0', 'output_1', 'output_2', 'output_3', 'output_4', 'output_5', 'output_6', 'output_7', 'output_8', 'output_9'],{"images:0":img}) This gives non zero outputs. However when running trt engine, the outputs are mostly 0. trt engine code: import numpy as np import tensorrt as trt import pycuda.autoinit import pycuda.driver as cuda import time, math   class TRTInference:     def __init__(self, trt_engine_path, trt_engine_datatype, net_type='EfficientNet'):         self.cfx = cuda.Device(0).make_context()         stream = cuda.Stream()          TRT_LOGGER = trt.Logger(trt.Logger.INFO)         trt.init_libnvinfer_plugins(TRT_LOGGER, '')         runtime = trt.Runtime(TRT_LOGGER)          # deserialize engine         with open(trt_engine_path, 'rb') as f:             buf = f.read()             engine = runtime.deserialize_cuda_engine(buf)         context = engine.create_execution_context()          # prepare buffer         host_inputs  = []         cuda_inputs  = []         host_outputs = []         cuda_outputs = []         bindings = []          for binding in engine:             size = trt.volume(engine.get_binding_shape(binding)) * engine.max_batch_size             host_mem = cuda.pagelocked_empty(size, np.float32)             cuda_mem = cuda.mem_alloc(host_mem.nbytes)              bindings.append(int(cuda_mem))             if engine.binding_is_input(binding):                 host_inputs.append(host_mem)                 cuda_inputs.append(cuda_mem)             else:                 host_outputs.append(host_mem)                 cuda_outputs.append(cuda_mem)          # store         self.stream  = stream         self.context = context         self.engine  = engine          self.host_inputs = host_inputs         self.cuda_inputs = cuda_inputs         self.host_outputs = host_outputs         self.cuda_outputs = cuda_outputs         self.bindings = bindings         self.net_type = net_type       def infer(self, image,result):         np.copyto(self.host_inputs[0], image.ravel())          # inference         start_time = time.time()         cuda.memcpy_htod_async(self.cuda_inputs[0], self.host_inputs[0], self.stream)         self.context.execute_async(bindings=self.bindings, stream_handle=self.stream.handle)         for i in range(len(self.cuda_outputs)):                 cuda.memcpy_dtoh_async(self.host_outputs[i], self.cuda_outputs[i], self.stream)                 self.stream.synchronize()         print(" execute times of "+ self.net_type +':' +str(time.time()-start_time)+'\n')                 result[self.net_type] = self.host_outputs       trt_engine=TRTInference('efficientdet-d0_nwonly.trt',trt_engine_datatype=trt.DataType.FLOAT,net_type='EfficientDet') result={} trt_engine.infer(2*np.ones((1,512, 512,3)),result) Attachments: efficientdet-d0_nwonly_trt.zip efficientdet-d0_nwonly_onnx.zip TRT version: 7.1.3.4 What might be the reason?

title: Misuse of ShuffleLayer or TrT could fuse this kind of pattern(consecutive shuffle layers)?
author: pmixer
body: Description As shuffle layer of a combination of pre-transpose+reshape+post-transpose, sometimes users may use separate shuffle layers for each reshape or transpose, which causing more shuffle layers added to the TrT network. title: Questions about int8 inference
body: Description Hi, I'm running a toy model with just a conv layer on TensorRT in int8 precision. I did the following according to the document:  Set the dynamic range of input and output. Set conv layer precision to int8. Set the output type of conv layer to int8. I couldn't find a way to set the type of network inputs, but it also seems not needed according to the document. Enabled int8 mode in builder. I also set strict_type_constraints = True because I want to make sure it runs on int8.  But then I saw some logs which are a little confusing. At the start my logger level was on WARNING and I saw the following. [TensorRT] WARNING: No implementation of layer conv obeys the requested constraints in strict mode. No conforming implementation was found i.e. requested layer computation precision and output precision types are ignored, using the fastest implementation.  To get more information, I set the logger level to VERBOSE and saw it's auto-tuning for the best tactics. However, I only saw like three types of format combination for conv layer and neither of them are int8 -> int8. Autotuning format combination: Float(3,672,1,150528) -> Float(16,3568,1,795664) Autotuning format combination: Float(1,224,50176,150528) -> Float(1,223,49729,795664) Autotuning format combination: Int8(1,224,50176:4,50176) -> Float(1,223,49729,795664)  A couple of questions I had are  From the format combination, does it mean for int8 inference conv layer takes in int8 input and generate float output? Do we have some documents about layer format combination support? Why would it generate the warning of "no implementation of layer conv obeys the requested ..."? Is it because I set the output type to int8 or maybe I didn't set the input type to int8? Is there a way to know what precision each layer is running on? How does TensorRT handle int8 <-> float conversion? For non-computation layers, here mentioned that they don't have int8 implementation, does it mean if the output from previous layer is int8 then those layers need to convert it to float first? Would this introduce some overheads?  Sorry to bother you guys with so many questions. Any help would be greatly appreciated! Environment TensorRT Version: 7.2.3 NVIDIA GPU: V100 NVIDIA Driver Version: 450.80.02 CUDA Version: 11.1

title: No heterogeneous precision implementation(FP16,FP32) of Fully Connected Layer in Tensorrt
author: ccjjs
body: Description Cuda FMA instruction( D = C + A*B ) has some implementation that do A*B in FP16 and accumelate the result to FP32. This produce more accurate result than that do accumelation in FP16. I tried to achieve this in tensorrt by setting precision mode of Fully Connected Layer to FP16 and Output type to FP32. cuda.pagelocked_empty(size, np.float32)             cuda_mem = cuda.mem_alloc(host_mem.nbytes)              bindings.append(int(cuda_mem))             if engine.binding_is_input(binding): title: Large discrepancies when creating Tensorrt engine in FP16 on transformer based model
author: zmy1116
body: Description Hello, I'm working on creating trt engine for TimeSformer. https://github.com/facebookresearch/TimeSformer I build the network use TensorRT python API and I can confirm the engine produce reasonable result in FP32. However, the FP16 engine produces results that is far with expected output. The main problem is that within each self attention block, the gelu function amplifies the discrepancies accumulated before, and since there are 12 blocks chained, eventually the discrepancy explode. The table below shows normalized discrepancy (normalized err is defined as norm(diff)/ norm(fp32_value)) between FP16 and FP32 on 6 different steps for each of 12 self-attention blocks:  after time self-attention after spatial self-attention after MLP - FC1 after MLP - GELU after MLP - FC2 output      T-attention  S-attention       FC1      GELU       FC2    output 0      0.000429     0.001589  0.001332  0.003152  0.003271  0.002415 1      0.002342     0.002767  0.001660  0.004542  0.004563  0.003427 2      0.003424     0.003747  0.002070  0.005539  0.006106  0.004365 3      0.004315     0.004391  0.002267  0.005573  0.007846  0.005714 4      0.005700     0.006732  0.003855  0.010994  0.023288  0.014126 5      0.013844     0.013440  0.007358  0.029005  0.058700  0.049154 6      0.049353     0.054302  0.102258  0.473737  0.535258  0.336202 7      0.335790     0.335395  0.139182  0.372451  0.702222  0.348630 8      0.348025     0.349228  0.183254  0.399796  0.538561  0.356199 9      0.355522     0.361621  0.401468  0.669973  0.805795  0.383704 10     0.381401     0.397778  0.706607  0.966223  0.910731  0.400721 11     0.441942     0.557325  0.280049  1.161975  1.132105  0.569143  You can see that GELU amplifies discrepancy from previous step 3x+ for every block, eventually the error goes to 100%+  Environment I used the ngc docker docker pull nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt:21.05-py3 TensorRT Version: 7.2.3.4 NVIDIA GPU: Tesla T4  ,    AWS  g4dn machine NVIDIA Driver Version:  440.64.00 CUDA Version:  11.3 CUDNN Version: Operating System:  ubuntu Python Version (if applicable): Tensorflow Version (if applicable): PyTorch Version (if applicable): Baremetal or Container (if so, version): Relevant Files I have created the following repository to reproduce the issue https://github.com/zmy1116/timesfromer_trtfp16_error Steps To Reproduce  # clone repo git clone https://github.com/zmy1116/timesfromer_trtfp16_error  cd timesfromer_trtfp16_error  # download pretrained weights from TimeSformer official repo wget https://www.dropbox.com/s/g5t24we9gl5yk88/TimeSformer_divST_8x32_224_K400.pyth  # build 2 models in fp32 and fp16, get the outputs and do comparison python conversions.py TimeSformer_divST_8x32_224_K400.pyth test_inputs.p result_fp32.p  python conversions.py TimeSformer_divST_8x32_224_K400.pyth test_inputs.p result_fp16.p --fp16_mode  # do comparison python compare.py  you should see the same error table i presented at the beginning. I think this is not a problem for specific model,   if raw scale of discrepancy is large, then gelu is going to amplfy it, after few blocks the results are certainly off.  I'm sort of surprised that you have not dealt this with BERT because I assume the same issue should happen on other transformer based model. Thanks

author: hao6699
body: Description  Environment TensorRT Version:  7.1.3.4 NVIDIA GPU:  RTX 2080TI NVIDIA Driver Version:  450.51.06 CUDA Version:  11.0 CUDNN Version:  8.0.4 Operating System: Ubuntu 18.04 Python Version (if applicable):  3.6.4 Tensorflow Version (if applicable): PyTorch Version (if applicable): Baremetal or Container (if so, version): Relevant Files  Steps To Reproduce  I have an ocr model,  which consists of a detection model and a recognition model. When an image come, it will first  through the detection model and produce many word images, then throw these word images into recognition model to get final result. I write a class for each model. Like this: import pycuda.driver as cuda import tensorrt as trt  class Detection:     def __init__(self, file_path):         self.file_path = file_path         self.cfx = cuda.Device(0).make_context()         self.stream = cuda.Stream()         self.trt_logger = trt.Logger(trt.Logger.INFO)         self.engine = self._load_engine()         self.context = self.engine.create_execution_context()      def _load_engine(self):         # Load serialized engine file into memory         with open(self.file_path, "rb") as f, trt.Runtime(self.trt_logger) as runtime:             return runtime.deserialize_cuda_engine(f.read())      def _allocate_buffers(self, image_pred):         pass      def run(self, image):        '''        image size is fixed        '''         self.cfx.push()         host_inputs, device_inputs, host_outputs, device_outputs = self._allocate_buffers(image)         for h_input, d_input in zip(host_inputs, device_inputs):             cuda.memcpy_htod_async(d_input, h_input.reshape(-1))         bindings = device_inputs + device_outputs         self.context.execute_async(batch_size=1, bindings=bindings, stream_handle=self.stream.handle)         for h_output, d_output in zip(host_outputs, device_outputs):             cuda.memcpy_dtoh_async(h_output, d_output)         self.stream.synchronize()         output = host_outputs[0]         return output  class Recognition:     def __init__(self, file_path):         self.file_path = file_path         self.cfx = cuda.Device(0).make_context()         self.stream = cuda.Stream()         self.trt_logger = trt.Logger(trt.Logger.INFO)         self.engine = self._load_engine()         self.context = self.engine.create_execution_context()      def _load_engine(self):         # Load serialized engine file into memory         with open(self.file_path, "rb") as f, trt.Runtime(self.trt_logger) as runtime:             return runtime.deserialize_cuda_engine(f.read())      def _set_bind_shapes(self, image):         pass      def run(self, image):         '''         image size is unfixed         '''         self.cfx.push()         host_inputs, device_inputs, host_outputs, device_outputs = self._set_bind_shapes(image)         for h_input, d_input in zip(host_inputs, device_inputs):             cuda.memcpy_htod_async(d_input, h_input.reshape(-1))         bindings = device_inputs + device_outputs         self.context.execute_async(batch_size=1, bindings=bindings, stream_handle=self.stream.handle)         for h_output, d_output in zip(host_outputs, device_outputs):             cuda.memcpy_dtoh_async(h_output, d_output)         self.stream.synchronize()         output = host_outputs[0]         return output  class OCR:     '''     integration model     '''     def __init__(self, craft_path, crnn_path):         cuda.init()         self.detection = Detection(craft_path)         self.recognition = Recognition(crnn_path)      def run(self, image):         results = []         boxes, images = self.detection.run(image)         for word_image in images:             h, w, _ = word_image.shape             pred_texts = self.recognition.run(word_image)             results.append(pred_texts)         return results  Multithread inference code is below: if __name__ == '__main__':     import cv2     import os     from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, wait          def handle_ocr(image):         return trt_ocr.run(image)     _ocr_pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4)     detection_path = 'detection_model.trt'     recognition_path = 'recognition_model.trt'     image_path = 'test_imgs'     trt_ocr = OCR(detection_path, recognition_path)     task_list = []     for img_name in os.listdir(image_path):         img = cv2.imread(os.path.join(image_path, img_name))         task = _ocr_pool.submit(handle_ocr, img)         task_list.append((img_name, task))     wait([task for _, task in task_list])  I run the code above, it will through these errors: [TensorRT] ERROR: ../rtSafe/cuda/caskConvolutionRunner.cpp (490) - Cuda Error in execute: 1 (invalid argument) [TensorRT] ERROR: FAILED_EXECUTION: std::exception [TensorRT] ERROR: myelin/myelinRunner.cpp (397) - Cuda Error in execute: 1 (invalid argument) [TensorRT] ERROR: FAILED_EXECUTION: std::exception  But it still get the right results, while sometimes it will throw different errors, and it collapses : pycuda._driver.LogicError: cuMemcpyDtoHAsync failed: an illegal memory access was encountered Even with the right results, the program will increasely occupies the gpu memory util OOM. Besides, when I separately run multithread inference with Detection class or Recognition class, it works well. So, I am very confused how to mutithread inference with muti-model like this case safely?  The point is that the two models are not unrelated, but the input of one model depends on the output of the other. Thanks !!!

title: New TensorRT release introduces NaNs in 3D Resnext on 16XX GPUs
author: dmenig
body:
Description With latest TensorRT docker image, some 3d models can't be used with GPUs 1650 up to 1660 Ti with FP16 precision anymore. Environment TensorRT Version:  7.0.0.1 -> 7.2.2.3 NVIDIA GPU: 1650 to 1660 Ti NVIDIA Driver Version: 465 Operating System: Ubuntu PyTorch Version (if applicable): 1.9.0 Steps To Reproduce I'm comparing both those images from NVCR : nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt:21.06-py3 and nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt:20.03-py3 nvidia-docker run -it nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt:2X.0X-py3 /bin/bash  Inside the container, get the repository for the model : git clone https://github.com/kenshohara/3D-ResNets-PyTorch.git cd 3D-ResNets-PyTorch  git checkout 35640f358c05904ab53816d8da0f2d968b4b3038 # current master is broken pip install torch torchvision sklearn  Export a simple resnet model python3 import torch import torchvision from models import resnext  dummy_input = torch.randn(1, 3, 35, 224, 224).float().cuda() model = resnext.resnet50(sample_size=224, sample_duration=35).eval().cuda()  with torch.no_grad():     torch.onnx.export(         model,         dummy_input,         "resnet.onnx",         verbose=True,     )   Then /usr/src/tensorrt/bin/trtexec --onnx=resnet.onnx --fp16 --workspace=500 --saveEngine=resnet.trt --inputIOFormats=fp32:chw --outputIOFormats=fp32:chw  Finally, do a simple forward pass to get output values : python3 import tensorrt as trt import pycuda.driver as cuda import pycuda.autoinit import os import sys import numpy as np  class HostDeviceMem(object):     def __init__(self, host_mem, device_mem):         self.host = host_mem         self.device = device_mem     def __str__(self):         return "Host:
" + str(self.host) + "
Device:
" + str(self.device)     def __repr__(self):         return self.__str__()    def allocate_buffers(engine):     inputs = []     outputs = []     bindings = []     stream = cuda.Stream()     for binding in engine:         size = trt.volume(engine.get_binding_shape(binding)) * engine.max_batch_size         dtype = trt.nptype(engine.get_binding_dtype(binding))         # Allocate host and device buffers         host_mem = cuda.pagelocked_empty(size, dtype)         device_mem = cuda.mem_alloc(host_mem.nbytes)         # Append the device buffer to device bindings.         bindings.append(int(device_mem))         # Append to the appropriate list.         if engine.binding_is_input(binding):             inputs.append(HostDeviceMem(host_mem, device_mem))         else:             outputs.append(HostDeviceMem(host_mem, device_mem))     return inputs, outputs, bindings, stream    def get_engine(engine_file_path=""):     """Attempts to load a serialized engine if available, otherwise builds a new TensorRT engine and saves it."""     assert os.path.exists(engine_file_path), "Engine file doesn't exist"     # If a serialized engine exists, use it instead of building an engine.     print("Reading engine from file {}".format(engine_file_path))     with open(engine_file_path, "rb") as f, trt.Runtime(TRT_LOGGER) as runtime:         return runtime.deserialize_cuda_engine(f.read())   TRT_LOGGER = trt.Logger()  engine_file_path="resnet.trt" with get_engine(     engine_file_path ) as engine, engine.create_execution_context() as context:     inputs, outputs, bindings, stream = allocate_buffers(engine)     # Do inference     # Set host input to the image. The do_inference function will copy the input to the GPU before executing.     np.random.seed(17)     inputs[0].host = np.array(         np.random.choice(range(256), (1, 3, 35, 224, 224)),         dtype=np.float32,     )     [cuda.memcpy_htod_async(inp.device, inp.host, stream) for inp in inputs]     context.execute_async_v2(bindings=bindings, stream_handle=stream.handle)     [         cuda.memcpy_dtoh_async(out.host, out.device, stream)         for out in outputs     ]     stream.synchronize()     print([out.host for out in outputs])   Using this with 21.06 gives nans, and normal floats with 20.03. Interestingly, reducing the duration to 16 and the image size to 112 fixes the problem.

title: No speedup in INT8 on 3D architecture with grouped convolutions
author: dmenig
body: Description I see no speedup between FP16 and INT8 on groupd convolution model. Environment TensorRT Version: 7.2.2.3 NVIDIA GPU: 2080 Ti (but I haven't seen any GPU that doesn't have the same problem, and I've truly tested most recent GPUs) NVIDIA Driver Version: 460.37 CUDA Version:  11.2 CUDNN Version: 8.1.0 Operating System: Ubuntu 20.04 Python Version (if applicable): 3.8 PyTorch Version (if applicable): 1.8.1 Relevant Files You can use a NVCR TensorRT container nvidia-docker run -it nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt:21.03-py3 /bin/bash  Get the repository for the group convolutions 3D model git clone https://github.com/kenshohara/3D-ResNets-PyTorch.git cd 3D-ResNets-PyTorch  git checkout 35640f358c05904ab53816d8da0f2d968b4b3038 # current master is broken pip install torch torchvision sklearn  Export a simple resnext model python3 import torch import torchvision from models import resnext  dummy_input = torch.randn(8, 3, 35, 224, 224).float().cuda()    ## Regular 3d model model = torchvision.models.video.r2plus1d_18().eval().cuda()   ## Resnext 3d model model = resnext.resnet101(sample_size=224, sample_duration=35).eval().cuda()  with torch.no_grad():     torch.onnx.export(         model,         dummy_input,         "resnet.onnx",         verbose=True,     )  Steps To Reproduce Use the script above to generate a onnx model. Then optimize it with this command : # FP16  optimization :  /usr/src/tensorrt/bin/trtexec --onnx=resnet.onnx --fp16 --workspace=5000 --saveEngine=resnet.trt --inputIOFormats=fp32:chw --outputIOFormats=fp32:chw  # INT8 (quantization) optimization :  /usr/src/tensorrt/bin/trtexec --onnx=resnet.onnx --best --workspace=5000 --saveEngine=resnet.trt --inputIOFormats=fp32:chw --allowGPUFallback --outputIOFormats=fp32:chw  Speedtest results are the following : GPU latencies in ms "Regular" 3d model : FP16 : 17.1 INT8 : 9.28  Resnext 3d model : FP16 : 11.4 INT8 : 11.5  So the optimization for INT8 quantization work for regular 3d convolutions but not for this specific model. INT8 expected speedup on any model should be about *2, am I right ? I believe that INT8 quantization of this kind of convolution might still not be supported in TensorRT, according to https://forums.developer.nvidia.com/t/does-tensorrt-support-conv3d-with-tensor-core/113193/9 If this is what is causing the problem, could you open a feature request so that this is solved when you guys have the time, please ?

title: question about how cuda context works
author: menglin0320
body: I'm trying to optimize the inference throughput for a model with dynamic input. the size difference between samples can be quite significant. So I want to avoid padding and do something similar to batching,  I want to run several samples concurrently with the same engine. The inference time will still be bottlenecked by the biggest sample in the batch but a lot of flops are saved, also it prevents possible performance drop from padding too much. From what I learned If works are in different cuda contexts there is no real parallel working, instead it is just better scheduling. Also one process can only have one cuda context and threads can share contexts.  But I didn't find anything talking about how to share one context among threads yet. When there is problem on context in a threading, most of the solutions just suggest to use Device.make_context()  There's not much difference between multithreading and multiprocess then. If each thread owns it's own context then there is no real concurrent work. Is my understanding right and anyone knows how to do the thing I want to do correctly. title: INT8 inference with TensorRT 8 with efficientdet-lite2 and efficientdet-lite1 detect nothing at all.
author: ethan28135
body: INT8 inference with TensorRT 8 with efficientdet-lite2 and efficientdet-lite1 in NVIDIA V100, Jetson Xavier NX and Jetson Xavier AGX detect nothing at all across all test images, no matter what image is fed in whether it is from coco dataset or outside coco dataset, with the exception that only in some situations, efficientdet-lite1 gives good detections for all test images if certain input resolutions, certain image input batch size, certain calibration batch size and certain calibration image files are used. This is kinda weird. By the way, I use images in coco train set to calibrate for INT8. I also used coco val set to calibrate, but the same problem happens. However, FP16 is always giving good detections no matter what settings and what images are used, so likely it is a problem with INT8, but I am not sure where is the problem. I did not modify any of the codes. Steps to reproduce (executing in Jupyter Notebook/Lab): min_score_thresh = 0.35 saved_model_dir = '/path/to/savedmodel' coco_trainset = 'train2017' // inspect.py is the code in google/automl repository !python model_inspect.py --runmode=saved_model  --model_name=efficientdet-lite2 --ckpt_path=efficientdet-lite2  --hparams="image_size=1280x720" --saved_model_dir={saved_model_dir} // create_onnx.py is the code in NVIDIA/TensorRT repository !python create_onnx.py      --input_shape '1,3,720,1280'      --saved_model {saved_model_dir}      --onnx /path/to/efficientdet-lite2.onnx // build_engine.py is the code in NVIDIA/TensorRT repository !python /path/to/TensorRT/samples/python/efficientdet/build_engine.py  --onnx /path/to/efficientdet-lite2.onnx  --engine /path/to/efficientdet-lite2-engine.trt  --precision int8 --workspace 32  --calib_cache /path/to/calibration-efficientdet-lite2.cache  --calib_input /path/to/{coco_trainset}  --calib_batch_size 8  --calib_num_images 5000 After that, I just use /path/to/TensorRT/samples/python/efficientdet/infer.py to perform inference. When generating onnx, changing from input_shape '1,3,720,1280' to '1,720,1280,3' or to multiple batch size such as '2,3,720,1280' do not solve the problem, but in FP16, these work perfectly well. Changing calib_batch_size and calib_num_images do not work as well. However, as mentioned, in some situations, INT8 efficientdet-lite1 gives good detections for all test images, provided if input_shape is '1,3,720,1280' and calib_batch_size is 1 and calib_num_images is 1000 and if certain calibration images in the coco train set are used (if you are lucky to choose the right 1000 images). But for efficientdet-lite2, no matter how, INT8 with trt engine gives no detections at all for all test images. This is kinda weird. I need INT8 because it is giving a lot speed boost compared to FP16. Please help on this. Thanks.

title: Missing implementation of "Sign" op from ONNX
author: tianyilim
body: Description I attempted to convert a TensorFlow model with the tf.atan2 op to ONNX using tf2onnx with opset >= 9, and subsequently to TensorRT. However, I encounter the error No importer registered for op: Sign. Attempting to import as plugin. when attempting to convert the model into TensorRT using trtexec. It seems that tf2onnx converts tf.atan2 to a bunch of sub-ops, which include the Sign ONNX op. I ran the following command. trtexec --onnx=./onnx_models/model_infer.onnx \ --plugins=./TensorRT/build/libPointNetOps.so \ --saveEngine=./TensorRT/model_infer.lib This is not surprising as the documentation for supported ops lists Sign from ONNX as unsupported. The definition of Sign looks fairly easy to implement, as it is mainly an element-wise operation. I don't mind trying to implement it myself as a custom plugin, but was wondering if there are any pitfalls or challenges that were encountered that preclude its addition. Thanks for the help! title: What are the steps under the trtexec latency test?
author: YukunXia
body: As mentioned in #1243, the end-to-end host latency includes the H2D memcpy, GPU computing, and D2H memcpy. However, when testing a YOLOv5 model deployed with TensorRT, trtexec prints a lower e2e host latency than the one from a C++ program. 6.8ms vs 10ms. The related issue and results were discussed here: wang-xinyu/tensorrtx#707. That C++ program evaluated the execution time of the doInference function: void doInference(IExecutionContext& context, cudaStream_t& stream, void **buffers, float* input, float* output, int batchSize) {     // DMA input batch data to device, infer on the batch asynchronously, and DMA output back to host     CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(buffers[0], input, batchSize * 3 * INPUT_H * INPUT_W * sizeof(float), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, stream));     context.enqueue(batchSize, buffers, stream, nullptr);     CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(output, buffers[1], batchSize * OUTPUT_SIZE * sizeof(float), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost, stream));     cudaStreamSynchronize(stream); } https://github.com/wang-xinyu/tensorrtx/blob/f7d224f9e4fb8ed30eb75f89063a2baef932aebb/yolov5/yolov5.cpp#L256-L262 auto start = std::chrono::system_clock::now(); doInference(*context, stream, buffers, data, prob, BATCH_SIZE); auto end = std::chrono::system_clock::now(); std::cout << std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start).count() << "ms" << std::endl; std::chrono::system_clock::now() shouldn't cost ~1ms to run. title: Incorrect calculations in GridAnchorGenerator, gridAnchorLayer for rectangular inputs
author: marcbelmont
body: Description If the input layer of an object detector is not square, libnvinfer_plugin does not produce the correct bounding boxes. An incomplete fix was committed to master with #679 by @rajeevsrao . But parts of it are not in master anymore. The issue was also discussed in #807. Environment  NVIDIA Jetson TX2  Jetpack 4.6 [L4T 32.6.1] NV Power Mode: MAXP_CORE_ARM - Type: 3 jetson_stats.service: active   Libraries:  CUDA: 10.2.300 cuDNN: 8.2.1.32 TensorRT: 8.0.1.6 Visionworks: 1.6.0.501 OpenCV: 4.1.1 compiled CUDA: NO VPI: ii libnvvpi1 1.1.12 arm64 NVIDIA Vision Programming Interface library Vulkan: 1.2.70    Relevant Files and Fix The following changes fix the issue. modified   plugin/common/kernels/gridAnchorLayer.cu                                                                                                                                         @@ -34,8 +34,10 @@ __launch_bounds__(nthdsPerCTA) __global__ void gridAnchorKernel(const GridAnchor                                                                                               * the image Every coordinate will go back to the pixel coordinates in the input image if being multiplied by                                                                                * image_input_size Here we implicitly assumes the image input and feature map are square                                                                                                    */                                                                                                                                                                                    -    float anchorStride = (1.0 / param.H);                                                                                                                                                  -    float anchorOffset = 0.5 * anchorStride;                                                                                                                                               +    float anchorStrideH = (1.0 / param.H);                                                                                                                                                 +    float anchorOffsetH = 0.5 * anchorStrideH;                                                                                                                                             +    float anchorStrideW = (1.0 / param.W);                                                                                                                                                 +    float anchorOffsetW = 0.5 * anchorStrideW;                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              int tid = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;                                                                                                                                            if (tid >= dim)                                                                                                                                                                        @@ -47,8 +49,8 @@ __launch_bounds__(nthdsPerCTA) __global__ void gridAnchorKernel(const GridAnchor                                                                                               const int h = currIndex / param.W;                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      // Center coordinates                                                                                                                                                                  -    float yC = h * anchorStride + anchorOffset;                                                                                                                                            -    float xC = w * anchorStride + anchorOffset;                                                                                                                                            +    float yC = h * anchorStrideH + anchorOffsetH;                                                                                                                                          +    float xC = w * anchorStrideW + anchorOffsetW;                                                                                                                                           modified   plugin/gridAnchorPlugin/gridAnchorPlugin.cpp                                                                                                                                     @@ -109,11 +109,13 @@ GridAnchorGenerator::GridAnchorGenerator(const GridAnchorParameters* paramIn, in                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           std::vector<float> tmpWidths;                                                                                                                                                               std::vector<float> tmpHeights;                                                                                                                                                     +        float featMapAspectRatio = (float) (mParam[0].H) / (float) (mParam[0].W);                                                                                                          +        // TODO: calculate the ratio with the input layer height and width instead.                                                                                                                       // Calculate the width and height of the prior boxes                                                                                                                                        for (int i = 0; i < mNumPriors[id]; i++)                                                                                                                                                    {                                                                                                                                                                                               float sqrt_AR = sqrt(aspect_ratios[i]);                                                                                                                                        -            tmpWidths.push_back(scales[i] * sqrt_AR);                                                                                                                                      +            tmpWidths.push_back(scales[i] * sqrt_AR * featMapAspectRatio);                                                                                                                              tmpHeights.push_back(scales[i] / sqrt_AR);                                                                                                                                              }                                                                                                                                                                                   Steps To Reproduce  Use a SSD object detection model with a rectangular input layer for example 400x300. Convert it to TensorRT like in https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT/tree/main/samples/python/uff_ssd. Do inference using the TensorRT model on an image. The x coordinates of the output bounding boxes are invalid.  Example of how the plugin is used when doing graph surgeon: gs.create_plugin_node(         name="MultipleGridAnchorGenerator",         op="GridAnchorRect_TRT",         minSize=0.2,         maxSize=0.95,         aspectRatios=[1.0, 2.0, 0.5, 3.0, 0.33],         variance=[0.1, 0.1, 0.2, 0.2],         featureMapShapes=[40, 23, 20, 12, 10, 6, 5, 3, 3, 2, 2, 1],         numLayers=6, )

body: Description I am trying to convert onnx to TensorRT with dynamic batch size. def build_engine():     print('start loading split model')     TRT_LOGGER = trt.Logger()     builder = trt.Builder(TRT_LOGGER)     network = builder.create_network(1 << int(trt.NetworkDefinitionCreationFlag.EXPLICIT_BATCH))     parser = trt.OnnxParser(network, TRT_LOGGER)     trt_config = builder.create_builder_config()     # trt_config.flags = 1 << int(trt.BuilderFlag.FP16)     with open('model.onnx', 'rb') as model:         parser.parse(model.read())     profile = builder.create_optimization_profile()     profile.set_shape("input", (1, in_chans, h, w), (5, in_chans, h, w), (10, in_chans, h, w))     trt_config.add_optimization_profile(profile)     trt_config.max_workspace_size = 1 << 30     engine = builder.build_engine(network, config=trt_config)     # context = engine.create_execution_context()     with open('model.trt', 'wb') as f:         f.write(engine.serialize())     print('Engine build complete for split model')     return engine  If I run the above code, TensorRT model is generated without any error. But if I increase the batch size in profile.set_shape("input", (1, in_chans, h, w), (5, in_chans, h, w), (10, in_chans, h, w)) I get cuda memory error. Is there a way to solve this issue?

title: Supporting 1D deconvolutions in TensorRT
author: alecgunny
body: Description Deconvolutions (or transposed convolutions depending on who you're asking) aren't supported in more recent versions of TensorRT (which I understand that the operator support matrix explicitly mentions). However, this operation was supported as of TRT 7.2.1, and it became a critical part of a low-latency pipeline my team works on, which is built on top of the 20.11 NGC container release (which runs 7.2.1.6). Unfortunately, we need to begin moving past Python 3.6, which limits our ability to continue to leverage TensorRT. For reference, in the repo linked to below I've included a repro using the 21.10 container. Are there any plans to extend support to this operator in upcoming releases, and if so is there any rough timeline? Environment TensorRT Version: 8.0.3.4 NVIDIA GPU: V100 16GB NVIDIA Driver Version: 465.19.01 CUDA Version: 11.4 CUDNN Version: Operating System: Ubuntu Python Version (if applicable): 3.8 Tensorflow Version (if applicable): PyTorch Version (if applicable): 1.10 Baremetal or Container (if so, version): Container, 21.10-py3 Relevant Files https://github.com/alecgunny/trt-env-repro Steps To Reproduce Full steps can be found in the README of the attached repo, with logs for both functioning and non-functioning cases included. The main issue seems to be that after the first deconvolution layer, TensorRT throws the error [network.cpp::setWeightsName::3013] Error Code 1: Internal Error (The given weights is not used in the network!)  which stops the rest of the network build, cutting subsequent layers off.

body: Description I try to compile a toy model developed in TF v2.6.0 with TensorRT via ONNX. The model includes a keras.layers.conv2D layer inside a tf.while_loop with fixed number of iterations. 0.5, dtype=tf.float32)          inputs = self.conv(inputs)          i = tf.constant(0) 	 	c = lambda i, inputs: tf.less(i, iters[0,0])         # c = lambda i, inputs: tf.less(i, iters)         r = tf.while_loop(c, self.loop, [i, inputs])          return r[0], r[1]       def loop(self, i, inputs):         inputs = self.conv(inputs)    #If this conv layer is commented out, the compilation works         inputs=tf.add(inputs,inputs)         print(i,'hallo')          return [tf.add(i, 1), inputs]  model = ToyModel_conv2D()  img = tf.random.uniform(shape=[1, 512, 768, 3])  i, codes = model.predict( [img] )  print('i:', i)  model.save('dynamicloop_toy_model_conv2D')  Conversion to ONNX (tf2onnx v1.9.2): python -m tf2onnx.convert --saved-model dynamicloop_toy_model_conv2D --opset 12 --output onnx_models/dynamicloop_toy_model_conv2D_opset12.onnx The ONNX model is given by onnx.zip Compilation with trtexec tool trtexec --workspace=5000 --onnx=onnx_models/dynamicloop_toy_model_conv2D_opset12.onnx --shapes=input_1:1x512x768x3 --saveEngine=trt_engines/dynamicloop_toy_model_conv2D_opset12.trt Error message: ModelImporter.cpp:775: ERROR: builtin_op_importers.cpp:611 In function importConv: [8] Assertion failed: inputs.at(2).is_weights() && "The bias tensor is required to be an initializer for the Conv operator"  The detailed output of TensorRT can be found in the txt-file trtexec_error_output.txt Tested TensorRT versions: 8.0.1 and 8.2.0 EA. title: Onnx model conversion - fallback to NoOp kind operation
author: tisma
body: Building the TRT engines from an onnx exported model could be very painful because of the unsupported operations. First of all, there are two separate list of supported operations:  one is the official onnx operators list second onnx-tensorrt operators list  When you develop the model, you're basically limited to the second one list if you want to use TensorRT, and the solution for the unsupported layers are custom plugins. On the other side, TF-TRT conversion approach gives you less utilization/speedup, but it is a fail-safe conversion since the unsupported operations will fallback to TF's one. That is IMHO better approach since it is guaranteed that conversion will success no matter if there are some unsupported operations. Is it possible to implement some kind of generic NoOp layer inside TensorRT that will be used when unsupported operation in onnx model is present? For example just to pass-through tensors, or add constant weights or anything that won't be harmful but still makes this conversion to succeed.

title: Huggingface demos use an older version (4.6.1) of transformers, which has a bug in the implementation of t5
author: sam-writer
body: The Huggingface/demos requirements file specifies transformers==4.6.1 It is my understanding from this PR in transformers that in 4.6.1 and before, T5's decoder used the encoder's attention mask when decoding and that the changes introduced in that PR (which show up in all versions of transformers>4.6.1) change the signature of T5 so that the decoder can have its own attention masking. (Note: I didn't use the normal issue template because this isn't really a bug in TRT, but it seems worth being aware of.)
